title: Smooth characteristic-$p$ Artin–Schreier calculation
statement:
Let $k$ be algebraically closed of characteristic $p>0$ and let $C$ be a
smooth separated finite-type scheme of dimension at most one. All
applicable assertions $\mathcal C_r(C,\underline{\mathbf F_p})$ hold.
For proper $C$, invariance under algebraically closed extension is induced
by the kernel of Frobenius minus the identity on $H^1(C,\mathcal O_C)$.

proof.text: Use the natural Ext/derived cohomology comparison to read the cited Ext long exact sequence in the derived cohomology groups used here. For a smooth connected one-dimensional component $D$, take the explicit Artin--Schreier row $0\to\underline{\mathbf F_p}\xrightarrow{i}G\xrightarrow{\wp}G\to0$, where $G=(\mathcal O_D)_{\mathrm{et}}$ and $\wp(s)=s^p-s$. The top coherent finiteness theorem applies at $d=1$ and makes $E=H^1(D,\mathcal O_D)$ finite-dimensional: $D$ is Noetherian by finite-type-over-Noetherian and its structure module is quasi-coherent of finite type, hence coherent by the locally Noetherian criterion. The scalar-comparison theorem identifies $H^1(D,G)$ additively with $E$ and identifies the cohomology of sectionwise multiplication by $c$ with multiplication by $c$ on $E$. Transfer the sectionwise Frobenius map $s\mapsto s^p$ through this identification to an additive map $F:E\to E$. The section identity $\mathrm{Fr}\mu_c=\mu_{c^p}\mathrm{Fr}$ implies $F(cv)=c^pF(v)$ after taking cohomology; additivity follows from $(s+t)^p=s^p+t^p$ and the cohomology construction on additive resolutions. Choose resolution lifts of Frobenius and the identity; their difference lifts $\wp$, and on cocycle classes its map is the difference of their maps. Thus $H^1(\wp)=F-1$. Semilinear surjectivity now makes $H^1(\wp)$ surjective. The Ga comparison/vanishing theorem says $H^q(D,G)=0$ for $q\geq2$. In the Artin--Schreier long exact sequence, surjectivity of $H^1(\wp)$ makes $H^2(D,\mathbf F_p)$ inject into $H^2(D,G)=0$. For $q>2$ both adjacent Ga terms vanish, so exactness gives $H^q(D,\mathbf F_p)=0$. This argument uses only a one-dimensional component and does not apply a connected-curve theorem to a point.

proof.text: Decompose $C$ as a finite disjoint union of smooth connected one-dimensional curves and copies of $\operatorname{Spec}k$ by the smooth-curve/points decomposition. Higher etale cohomology of each point component is zero by geometric-point cohomology. Constant-sheaf inverse-image identifies the coefficients on every component with its constant $\mathbf F_p$ sheaf. The canonical finite-coproduct restriction isomorphisms therefore give $H^q(C,\mathbf F_p)=0$ for all $q\geq2$ by step 1 and the point calculation. This proves (1), (2) and (3), including empty index sets. For any open immersion $a:W\hookrightarrow C$, identify $W$ with its open image. Finite-type-over-Noetherian and Noetherian-open inheritance show that $W$ is quasi-compact. In an affine chart $\operatorname{Spec}A$ of $C$, every point of $W$ has a distinguished neighbourhood $\operatorname{Spec}A_f$ contained in $W$. Since $A$ is a finitely generated $k$-algebra, adjoining the single generator $f^{-1}$ makes $A_f$ finitely generated; quasi-compactness gives finitely many such neighbourhoods covering $W$. This verifies finite type directly from its affine-cover definition. The diagonal of $W$ is the restriction of the closed diagonal of $C$ to $W\times_kW$, cut out locally by the same defining ideal, hence is closed; thus $W$ is separated. Smoothness restricts by the cited smooth-open theorem, and the cited open-subspace dimension theorem gives $\dim W\leq1$. Consequently the preceding decomposition/vanishing argument applies also to $W$, and constant-sheaf inverse-image identifies $a^{-1}\mathbf F_p$ with $\mathbf F_{p,W}$. Both source and target of the actual restriction in (8) are zero, so it is surjective. The empty scheme has the empty product, the zero abelian group.

proof.text: Use the natural Ext/derived cohomology comparison to read the cited Ext long exact sequence in the derived cohomology groups used here. For the affine calculation, apply Artin--Schreier directly on $C$ and affine quasi-coherent acyclicity to $G=(\mathcal O_C)_{\mathrm{et}}$. Exactness gives $H^1(C,\mathbf F_p)\cong\Gamma(C,\mathcal O_C)/(F-1)\Gamma(C,\mathcal O_C)$ and $H^q(C,\mathbf F_p)=0$ for $q>1$. No surjectivity of $F-1$ on this generally infinite-dimensional ring is used.

proof.text: Use the natural Ext/derived cohomology comparison to read the cited Ext long exact sequence in the derived cohomology groups used here. Assume $C$ proper; connectedness is not assumed. Let $E_q=H^q(C,\mathcal O_C)$. Proper coherent finiteness makes each $E_q$ finite-dimensional over $k$; $\mathcal O_C$ is coherent since a finite-type scheme over a field is Noetherian. The Frobenius comparison node identifies $H^q(C_{\mathrm{et}},G)$ with $E_q$ and $H^q(\wp)$ with $F_q-1$: subtract resolution lifts of Frobenius and the identity, then evaluate on cocycle classes. Here $F_q$ is $p$-linear; $F_q-1$ is additive. The semilinear surjectivity theorem makes $F_q-1$ surjective. In the Artin--Schreier long exact sequence, the connecting map after $H^{q-1}(\wp)$ is therefore zero, so $H^q(i)$ is injective with image $\ker(F_q-1)$, for $q=1$; in degree zero injectivity is left exactness. Consequently the actual inclusion maps induce canonical isomorphisms $H^q(C,\mathbf F_p)\cong E_q^{F_q}$ for $q=0,1$. The fixed-point finiteness theorem makes these groups finite. Step 2 makes every group in degree $q\geq2$ zero, proving (5), and gives $H^2(C,\mathbf F_p)=\operatorname{coker}(F_1-1)=0$. In particular the degree-one identification is with the Frobenius-fixed part of the actual coherent cohomology, not just an unspecified finite-vector-space model.

proof.text: For an algebraically closed extension $k\subseteq k'$, let $j:C_{k'}\to C$ be the projection. The base-change-curve statement preserves smoothness, properness and the dimension bound, so step 4 applies also to $C_{k'}$. Ring pullback commutes with $s\mapsto s^p-s$ and the constants inclusion; the Artin--Schreier pullback-rows node provides the morphism $u:j^{-1}G\to G'$ and the equality $u\circ j^{-1}i=i'$, where the target row uses the inverse-image constant sheaf. Identify it with the constant sheaf on $C_{k'}$ by constant-sheaf inverse-image; its constants inclusion sends the same residue class to the same prime-field section, so it is the Artin--Schreier inclusion used in step 4. Cohomology pullback naturality then gives $H^q(i')\rho^q=H^q(u)j^*H^q(i)$ for $q=0,1$. Under the coherent comparison node, the right hand side sends $v$ to $b_q(v\otimes1)$ and carries Frobenius to the semilinear tensor extension $F'_q(v\otimes a)=F_q(v)\otimes a^p$. Thus the canonical kernel identifications of step 4 carry $\rho^q$ precisely to $E_q^{F_q}\to(E_q\otimes_kk')^{F'_q}$, $v\mapsto v\otimes1$. The fixed-point invariance theorem makes this map an isomorphism for $q=0,1$; in higher degrees both sides vanish by step 2. This proves (7) with the specified degree-one comparison map. It does not identify Frobenius with a $k'$-linear tensor extension: the $p$-power on the scalar is essential.

proof.text: Read the conjunction using the eight-assertions definition: steps 2--5 establish (1), (2), (3), (5), (7) and (8) whenever their stated hypotheses apply. For (4) and (6) the additional prime-to-characteristic hypothesis cannot hold for the nonzero constant $\mathbf F_p$ sheaf on a nonempty $C$: at every geometric point its fibre is the group $\mathbf F_p$, and an integer prime to $p$ acts invertibly, hence cannot annihilate that group. On the empty scheme the constant sheaf and its cohomology are zero and the conclusions hold. Thus these two implications introduce no affine field-extension invariance claim. This gives every applicable assertion for the stated curve and constant sheaf.
